subsystems.name: Host chassis
subsystems.role: the yeast cell itself, engineered to redirect carbon away from its own growth and toward the desired product.
parts: gene deletions to block competing pathways

subsystems.name: Genetic toolkit
subsystems.role: the molecular tools used to insert, delete or tune genes in the yeast genome.

subsystems.name: Metabolic pathway
subsystems.role: the set of enzymes that convert sugars into the target fuel or chemical.

subsystems.name: Fermentation system
subsystems.role: the bioreactor and conditions that keep the yeast alive and producing at high yield.

subsystems.name: Downstream processing
subsystems.role: separates the product from the broth and purifies it to market grade.

subsystems.name: Feedstock supply
subsystems.role: provides the sugars that feed the yeast, ideally from non-food or waste sources.

buildSteps.title: Choose the target molecule
buildSteps.detail: Select a fuel or chemical with a known or plausible biosynthetic route, and map the enzymes needed to make it from the yeast's natural metabolites.

buildSteps.title: Design genetic constructs
buildSteps.detail: Optimise gene sequences for yeast codon usage, choose promoters of different strengths, and assemble the pathway into a vector or genome-integration cassette.

buildSteps.title: Transform and edit yeast
buildSteps.detail: Introduce the DNA into yeast cells using chemical or electroporation methods, and use CRISPR to delete native genes that compete for carbon or degrade the product.

buildSteps.title: Screen and evolve strains
buildSteps.detail: Test many colonies for product titre, then use adaptive laboratory evolution or iterative rounds of editing to improve growth and yield.

buildSteps.title: Optimise fermentation
buildSteps.detail: Grow the best strain in small bioreactors, tuning sugar feed rate, oxygen, temperature and pH to maximise productivity and minimise by-products.

buildSteps.title: Scale up to pilot
buildSteps.detail: Run the process in progressively larger tanks (hundreds to thousands of litres), solving mixing, heat removal and contamination problems along the way.

buildSteps.title: Recover and purify
buildSteps.detail: Separate the yeast cells, then use distillation, extraction or membranes to isolate the product, and recycle water and solvents where possible.

prerequisites.why: building and testing many pathway variants requires cheap, fast construction of long DNA sequences.
redirecting yeast metabolism without harming growth depends on targeted gene deletions and insertions.
models predict where carbon will flow, but they cannot yet fully predict toxicity or regulation in engineered strains.
large-scale sterile bioreactors and downstream equipment are already used for ethanol, enzymes and antibiotics.
many target fuels are toxic to yeast above low concentrations, limiting titre and requiring costly separation.
sugar from crops competes with food; lignocellulosic and waste sugars are harder to break down and ferment.

pathway.milestone: commercial yeast fermentation for ethanol, lactic acid and a few specialty chemicals
pathway.unlocks: a base of industrial experience and equipment.

pathway.milestone: pilot-scale drop-in biofuels and complex molecules from engineered yeast
pathway.unlocks: products that fit existing fuel infrastructure without blending limits.
lower cost and no competition with food crops.

pathway.milestone: fully synthetic yeast genomes (e.g. the international Sc2.0 project) and cell-free biosynthesis
pathway.unlocks: faster design cycles and the ability to make molecules that no natural cell can produce.
